item.title: After ‘Boston,’ Where Does Stella Lefty Go?
item.description: The pop-country upstart workshopped a song on TikTok that became one of the year’s biggest hits. But crowdsourcing can only take a live show so far.

item.media:description: Stella Lefty’s rise has been fueled in part by her savvy attention to crowdsourced consensus.

item.title: Raye, Rosalía and Ella Langley Top a Women-Led 2027 Grammys Field
item.description: Langley is the first straight-up country artist to contend for the top album prize in eight years, and Raye’s 11 nods lead all nominees.

item.title: The Philharmonic and Met Opera Duel With Back-to-Back ‘Toscas’

item.title: Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker Comes Full Circle, Spinning to Philip Glass
item.description: In “GLA55,” the Belgian choreographer Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker revisits her minimalist roots with a gritty rearrangement of Glass’s early scores.

item.title: ‘The Fantasticks’ Review: A Gender Swap for a Still-Tender Story
item.description: Now two men play the young lovers in this long-running musical from 1960. Its quaint nostalgia remains intact for this Broadway production.

item.title: 2027 Grammy Snubs and Surprises: Madonna, Noah Kahan, Audrey Hobert and More
item.description: Madonna and Kahan were locked out of nominations in the top categories, the Womack Sisters were recognized and country’s gender divide showed up in an unexpected way.

item.media:description: Rosalía’s operatic track “Berghain” is a surprising entry in the song and record of the year categories.

item.title: Grammy Nominations 2027: See the Full List
item.description: The artists, albums and songs up for honors at the 69th annual ceremony were announced Monday. The show will be held on Feb. 7 in Los Angeles and air on ABC and Disney+ after decades on CBS.

item.title: South Korea to Examine How K-Pop Industry Treats Underage Performers
item.description: The announcement came after a New York Times investigation about the restrictive contracts of the group NewJeans, signed when its members were 14 to 17.
item.dc:creator: Jin Yu Young and Sarah Hurtes
item.media:description: NewJeans at the Billboard Women in Music Awards in Inglewood, Calif., in 2024. The group tried to quit its label over allegations of mistreatment.

item.title: A New Festival Embraces the Possibilities of Disability-Centered Opera
item.description: The three works at the Makemake festival at National Sawdust make the case that disability-led opera is artistically ambitious, despite the logistical challenges.
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Ferrari
item.media:credit: Ye Fan for The New York Times
item.media:description: The mezzo-soprano Hailey McAvoy at a rehearsal for “Sensorium Ex” in Brooklyn. McAvoy, who has cerebral palsy, also has created a music-theater piece, “Wholly Unwinding,” for the makemake festival.

item.title: A Mexican Artist Sang Some of His Hits. Authorities Stopped the Show, Then Arrested Him.
item.description: A concert by the singer Gabito Ballesteros was suspended after he sang songs that supposedly glorify cartel culture. The action has renewed a debate over culture and free speech.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner
item.media:description: Gabito Ballesteros performing in Mexico City in September.

item.title: Richard Sterban, the Bass Singer for the Oak Ridge Boys, Dies at 83
item.description: Mr. Sterban, who was a backup vocalist for Elvis Presley, was a singer of extraordinary range and power who could hit notes so low they could only be felt.
item.dc:creator: Bill Friskics-Warren
item.category: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
item.media:description: Richard Sterban of the Oak Ridge Boys performing in Nashville in 2023. His reverberating vocals galvanized the group’s hit version of “Elvira” in 1981.

item.title: Asia’s Eurovision Contest Is Missing China, India, Pakistan, Indonesia and Japan
